label: Rational Expressions
overview: A rational expression is a fraction where the numerator and/or denominator are polynomials. SAT questions ask you to simplify by canceling common factors, multiply or divide rational expressions, and identify values that make the expression undefined. Factoring is the key step in nearly every rational expression problem.

steps.title: Factor numerator and denominator
steps.content: x² − 9 is a difference of squares. x² − x − 6 factors as (x−3)(x+2).

commonMistakes.fix: You can only cancel a factor that multiplies the entire numerator or denominator. Terms added together cannot be canceled individually.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting to state excluded values after canceling
commonMistakes.fix: If (x−3) is canceled, note that x ≠ 3 (the original denominator was zero there).

quickTip: Always factor completely before trying to cancel. Trying to cancel before factoring is the most common error on rational expression problems.
